name: ISO 9001 quality management certification
summary: Quality management system certification: current edition, scope, independent assessment and transition questions.
currentStatus: ISO lists the 2026 edition as published and the 2015 edition as withdrawn.
applicability: Organizations across sectors may use the quality management standard. Certification is voluntary under the standard; customer contracts or other rules can create separate requirements.
exemptions: No universal business license is created by ISO 9001. Establish the intended QMS scope and assess any exclusions against the applicable edition.
application: Define the quality management system scope, implement it, and select an independent certification body if certification is needed. ISO does not issue certificates.
renewal: Confirm surveillance, recertification and the 2015-to-2026 transition arrangements with the certification body. No universal transition deadline is asserted here.
fees: Certification costs require a scope-specific quote from the certification body; buying the standard is a separate cost.

documents.text: Record the QMS scope, relevant products/services and the edition to be assessed.

name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: A framework for organizing cybersecurity risk outcomes, profiles and improvement priorities.
currentStatus: NIST publishes CSF 2.0 and supporting implementation resources.
applicability: Organizations of any size and sector can use CSF to manage cybersecurity risk. Adoption is generally voluntary; a contract or sector-specific rule may reference it.
exemptions: CSF is an outcomes framework, not a government business license. Applicability of separate regulations is outside this overview.
application: Define the organizational context, build a Current Profile, choose a Target Profile and prioritize gaps. Use the official quick-start guides and reference tools.
renewal: There is no NIST-issued CSF certificate to renew. Review the profile as risks, services and business needs change.
fees: NIST framework resources are available from the official website. Optional third-party consulting and assessment arrangements are separate.

name: Cyber Essentials certification
summary: UK cybersecurity certification scheme covering five technical control areas and two assurance levels.
currentStatus: Active NCSC scheme delivered through IASME and licensed certification bodies.
applicability: Organizations seeking baseline cyber security assurance, including suppliers whose customers require it. Check the contract and scope rather than assuming every UK business must certify.
exemptions: The scheme does not create a blanket statutory licensing obligation. Contractual requirements and scope exclusions must be checked separately.
application: Use IASME or a licensed certification body. Cyber Essentials uses an assessed self-assessment; Cyber Essentials Plus adds technical testing of the same control areas.
renewal: Confirm the certificate expiry date and current renewal requirements with IASME or the selected certification body before relying on a certificate.
fees: Current pricing depends on the scheme route and organization; use the official scheme quote or pricing page.

Decide whether the requesting customer needs Cyber Essentials or Cyber Essentials Plus.
